prior_findings_motivating_this_test.interpretation: Naive feature concatenation causes strong context interference; XRS retains a possible positive signal while proton context improves ranking but destabilizes thresholded decisions.

hypotheses: Restricting fit support to the SDO/HMI era reduces source-regime mismatch on recent forecasts.
Late fusion of separately learned solar and XRS probabilities reduces destructive modality interference relative to feature concatenation.
Adding a separately learned proton probability to late fusion either adds robust information or is rejected without further proton architecture search.

training_scopes.ALL_HISTORY: all eligible development rows before the fixed monitor start
training_scopes.SDO_HMI_ERA: eligible rows at or after 2010-05-01 and before the fixed monitor start

fixed_monitor.use: development monitor only; cannot become fresh final evidence

within_scope_split.method: hardened contiguous event and seven-day quiet units

model_contract.stacker: L2 logistic regression C=1.0 on calibration-role component logits only
model_contract.threshold_selection: maximum TSS on threshold role with lowest-threshold tie break

decision_rule: A mechanism is promising only if it improves TSS on the within-scope inner score and does not materially worsen matched-detection FAR; the already-inspected 2023-2025 monitor is corroborative development evidence only. No final superiority claim is allowed from this experiment.
